title: SLO Decision Ledger and Degradation Contract — Service-Level Hedging Playbook
author: Asha Rivera
body:
Overview
-------
This playbook establishes the 'SLO Decision Ledger' and a formal "degradation contract" for Redwood Inference services. It codifies how we: 1) accept and record SLO decisions, 2) automate graded degradations tied to real-time error-budget economics, 3) coordinate capacity hedging, and 4) collect incident evidence for postmortem and remediation. The goal is to keep customer-facing latency and availability predictable while preserving the ability to gracefully degrade non-critical functionality when capacity is constrained.

Intended audience
-----------------
- SREs owning service SLOs and capacity planning
- Service owners and product engineers for model-serving products
- Oncall responders and incident commanders
- Platform engineers implementing autoscale and routing policies

Key concepts
------------
- SLO Decision Ledger: single source-of-truth (Confluence + Git) recording SLO attributes and rationale for changes. Entries must include owner, reason, expected headroom, and rollback criteria.
- Degradation Contract: machine-readable policy that maps SLO burn state + capacity signals -> deterministic degradation actions (e.g., reduce streaming tokens, fallback to cheaper model, shed background reranking).
- Hedging: reserving soft headroom and warm pools for critical tenants when forecasted burn or surge is detected.

SLO Decision Ledger schema (required fields)
-------------------------------------------
A record must include the following (example as a header table in the ledger):
| field | description | example |
|-----|-----|-----|
| service_name | canonical service id | inference-router-prod |
| slo_id | short id | INF-P99-LAT |
| metric | metric name & query | request_p99_latency_ms |
| target | target value | <= 300ms |
| measurement_window | rolling window | 30d |
| error_budget | monthly allowed violation | 0.5% (monthly) |
| owner | primary responsible | eng-sre-model-serving |
| rationale | why this SLO was chosen | UX latency / SLAs with key customers |
| headroom_commit | reserved capacity/headroom | 15% reserved GPU pool |
| rollback_criteria | when to revert SLO changes | sustained error budget burn < 0.5x for 7d |

Admission checklist (pre-deploy)
-------------------------------
1. Ledger entry created with required fields and reviewer approval.
2. Canary and synthetic traffic configured: p99 and p95 probes aligned with production distribution.
3. Observability hooks: request/response traces, token counts, model-version tags.
4. Degradation contract reviewed: all non-critical features annotated for safe shedding.
5. Capacity plan: autoscale profile + warm-pool targets computed and approved.

Degradation contract structure (example YAML snippet)
--------------------------------------------------
# Machine-readable policy consumed by our routing/orchestrator
policy_version: v1
priority_classes: [critical, interactive, background]
triggers:
  - name: elevated-burn
    condition: |
      error_budget_burn_rate > 1.5 or forecasted_headroom_pct < 10
    actions:
      - type: reduce_model_variant
        params: { from: "llama-70b-q4", to: "llama-13b-q4" }
      - type: reduce_max_tokens
        params: { percent: 30 }
      - type: enable_queueing
        params: { max_inflight: 2000 }
  - name: critical-burn
    condition: |
      error_budget_burn_rate > 3.0 or forecasted_headroom_pct < 5
    actions:
      - type: enable_fallback_region
        params: { to_region: "secondary-eu" }
      - type: shed_background_work
        params: { features: ["reranking","explainer"] }

Operational thresholds and interpretations
-----------------------------------------
- Normal: error_budget_burn_rate <= 1.0 — normal operations, no automated degradation.
- Elevated: 1.0 < burn_rate <= 3.0 — automated graded degradations allowed (see policy).
- Critical: burn_rate > 3.0 — protective measures, SRE intervention required.
- If latency p99 breaches target for > 15 minutes AND burn_rate > 2.0, escalate to oncall-incident.

Prometheus alert examples (for implementation)
----------------------------------------------
- Error-rate alert (rate of 5xx or model failures):
  expr: sum(rate(inference_request_errors_total[2m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[2m])) > 0.01
  for: 5m
  labels: { severity: "page" }
  annotations: { runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-decision-ledger-and-degradation-contract-2026" }

- Error-budget burn-rate (1h window):
  expr: (rate(error_budget_spend[1h]) / rate(allocated_error_budget[1h])) > 1.5
  for: 10m

Capacity hedging and warm pools
-------------------------------
Guidelines:
- Critical services must reserve a warm pool of inference instances equivalent to 5-20% of peak RPS depending on model startup cost.
- Warm pools should be instrumented for instant routing (<= 30s) and KV-cache priming workflows.
- Hedging triggers: forecasted demand > 85% of soft capacity for 10m OR sudden headroom drop > 10% in 5m.

Autoscale policy example (Kubernetes HPA-like pseudocode)
-------------------------------------------------------
min_replicas: 4
max_replicas: 200
metrics:
  - type: rps
    target: 2500
  - type: p99_latency_ms
    scale_out_if: ">300"
  - type: queue_depth
    scale_out_if: ">1000"
scaling_cooldown_seconds: 60
prewarm_provision_seconds: 300

Oncall play steps (runtime hedging)
----------------------------------
1. Triage: confirm alerts and check SLO Decision Ledger entry for the service.
2. Evaluate burn rate and forecast: run `./tools/eb-forecast --service inference-router-prod --window 1h` (example CLI).
3. If elevated (1.0-3.0): enable degradation contract staged actions (automated via orchestrator). Document activation in the ledger with a timestamp.
4. If critical (>3.0) or customer impact observed: execute emergency steps (below) and page Tier 2/3.

Emergency steps (if automated degradations insufficient)
------------------------------------------------------
1. Enable immediate fallback routes: `orchestrator route-set --service inference-router-prod --to-region secondary-eu`
2. Preempt background queues: `taskctl pause --queue reranking`
3. Drop heavy requests at ingress using token-priority filters: `ingressctl set-policy --service inference-router-prod --policy token_priority`
4. If p99 remains > target after 10 minutes, roll back recent model or config change: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-server --to-revision=stable`
5. Record every action in the incident timeline and SLO Decision Ledger.

Incident evidence & postmortem standards
---------------------------------------
Required artifacts for post-incident review (attach to incident ticket):
- SLO Decision Ledger snapshot (immutable entry)
- Prometheus graphs: p95/p99 latency, error rates, headroom, GPU/utilization, queue depth (30m pre-incident, during, 24h post)
- Sample request/response traces (redacted) for 20 representative failures
- Degradation contract activation logs and orchestrator audit trail
- List of recent deploys and config changes (last 72h)
- Customer-facing impact log (tenants affected, routes impacted)

Evidence taxonomy (labels to attach to each artifact)
| artifact | label | retention |
|---|---:|---|
| ledger_snapshot | ledger | 2y |
| metrics_snapshot | telemetry | 90d |
| traces | pii_redacted | 180d |
| orchestration_logs | audit | 1y |

Postmortem sequencing (minimum required steps)
1. Incident triage and timeline construction within 48 hours.
2. Draft postmortem with hypothesis and data within 5 business days.
3. Blameless review with stakeholders and assignment of action items within 10 business days.
4. SLO Decision Ledger update (if SLO or headroom changes are approved) and follow-up verification (canary + synthetic) scheduled.

Tooling & automation hooks
-------------------------
- Ledger automation: PR-based ledger changes required. PR template must include 'slo-impact' and 'headroom-estimate' checkboxes.
- Orchestrator: accepts degradation-contract YAML and exposes a /policy/evaluate API.
- Hedging service: `hedge-agent` runs forecasting; exposes events to pagerduty and populates `forecasted_headroom_pct`.
- Observability: dashboards must include a single-pane 'SLO Health' with error-budget burn, p99, headroom, and warm-pool utilization.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Primary owner: eng-sre-model-serving (SRE team)
- Secondary: platform-orchestration (autoscale & policy enforcement)
- Quarterly governance: SLO review board (product + SRE + customer success) re-evaluates high-impact SLOs and headroom allocations.

Metrics to track for continuous improvement
-----------------------------------------
- Time between ledger entry and first enforcement test (goal < 7 days)
- Mean time from elevated burn alert to degradation contract activation (target < 5 minutes with automation)
- Frequency of manual emergency escalations per quarter (target: decreasing trend)
- False-positive degradations (unnecessary shedding) rate (target < 2% of activations)

Appendix: example CLI snippets and JSON payloads
------------------------------------------------
# Forecast command (example):
$ ./tools/eb-forecast --service inference-router-prod --window 1h --output json
{
  "service": "inference-router-prod",
  "forecasted_headroom_pct": 8.4,
  "error_budget_burn_rate": 2.1
}

# Orchestrator policy activation API
POST /policy/evaluate
Content-Type: application/json
{ "service": "inference-router-prod", "policy_version": "v1" }

# Example runbook log entry (one-line)
2026-02-09T14:03Z | action=enable_degradation | actor=hedge-agent | policy=degradation-v1 | reason=forecasted_headroom_pct<10
